notes: Authors may upload a single PDF (text + figures/tables combined) or a Word file with separate figure files, from which bioRxiv's automated engine builds a single PDF.
LaTeX/TeX source is not accepted directly; it must be converted to PDF before submission.
No word limit, page limit, font, margin, line-spacing, or line-numbering requirements are stated for initial submission.
No formatting/template is required; bioRxiv performs no typesetting.
PowerPoint files are also accepted for figures.
PICT, Bitmap, Excel, and PSD figure formats are not compatible and must be converted to PDF or another accepted format.
No figure count limit, resolution/dpi requirement, or dimension limit is stated in the guidelines.
Supplemental material is accepted in a wide range of file formats and is posted as-is (not required to be combined into a single PDF).
Large datasets should be deposited in an appropriate community database (e.g. PDB, GenBank) rather than uploaded as supplementary material.

Manuscripts must be complete but unpublished; case reports, narrative reviews, editorials, opinion pieces, tool announcements without data, protocols alone, hypotheses without data, teaching materials, theses, individual figures/tables, white papers, and guidelines are not accepted.
Clinical papers should be submitted to medRxiv instead of bioRxiv.
Authors classify each submission by subject category (e.g. Biochemistry, Genetics, Neuroscience) and by result type: New Results, Confirmatory Results, or Contradictory Results.
A competing-interests declaration is collected as part of the submission metadata.
Authors select a distribution license: CC BY, CC BY-NC, CC BY-ND, CC BY-NC-ND, CC0, or no reuse.
All submissions undergo basic screening for offensive/non-scientific content, plagiarism, and dual-use research concerns.
Revisions may be submitted at any time until journal publication; each revision keeps the same DOI with prior versions remaining accessible in the article history.
A single PDF containing text and any figures/tables is the preferred submission format.
A Word file may be submitted with figures as separate files; medRxiv auto-converts submissions to PDF.
TeX/LaTeX files must be converted to PDF by the author before submission; native LaTeX source is not accepted.
No maximum file size, word count, or page limit is stated in the submission guide or FAQ.

Not accepted: case reports/case series, narrative reviews, editorials, letters, opinion pieces without new data, preclinical or veterinary work, tool/service announcements, protocols without meta-analyses, hypotheses without new data, theses, guidelines, or policy statements.
Manuscripts must be unpublished, or submitted concurrently with a journal submission; already-published or already-accepted work will not be posted.
Identifying photographs of individuals (faces or other identifying features) must be removed, even if pixelated or blurred.

Ethics: authors must confirm 'all relevant ethical guidelines have been followed, all necessary IRB and/or ethics committee approvals have been obtained', and medRxiv requires 'a statement of ethical oversight by an independent dedicated oversight body' for any research involving human subjects, samples, or data (including anonymized data and surveys) unless the data are already publicly available.

Clinical trials must be 'registered with an internationally recognized trial registry', specifically 'a trial ID from an ICMJE-recognized trial registry (such as clinicaltrials.gov)', or provide documented exemption.
Funding statement required 'with details of all funding that supported the work'.
Competing interests declaration is mandatory.

Data availability statement required, covering 'the availability of all data referred to in the manuscript'; large datasets should be deposited in an appropriate repository (e.g. PDB, GenBank, NIH databases) rather than posted to medRxiv itself.
PRISMA guidelines are recommended (not stated as mandatory) for systematic reviews with meta-analyses: 'We recommend using PRISMA guidelines'.
Use of AI tools in manuscript preparation must be detailed in the manuscript, with authors accountable for accuracy and originality of AI-assisted content.
PRISMA reporting is recommended for systematic reviews.
Accepted formats for figures/images submitted as separate files: GIF, TIFF, EPS, JPEG, and PowerPoint.
Incompatible formats requiring conversion before submission: PICT, Bitmap, Excel, PSD.
No dpi, file-size, pixel-dimension, or figure-count limits are stated on the submission guide or FAQ pages.
Avoid images with partially or completely transparent backgrounds; they will not display correctly.
No photographs with identifiable individual faces are permitted, even pixelated or blurred versions.
Common word-processing/spreadsheet formats acceptable for tables submitted as separate files; no further structural requirements stated.
Supplemental files may use 'a wide range of popular file formats' with accessible content; additional tables and MPEG files are explicitly mentioned as acceptable supplementary content.
Large datasets should be deposited in an appropriate scientific repository (e.g. PDB, GenBank, NIH sites) rather than submitted to medRxiv as supplementary material.

medRxiv covers preprints 'in the medical, clinical, and related health sciences'; content types out of scope include case reports, narrative/scoping reviews without meta-analysis, editorials, letters, opinion pieces without data, laboratory protocols, theses, and manuscript components.
All submissions undergo basic screening for offensive/non-scientific content and plagiarism; content posing health risks or dual-use research of concern is flagged.
Authors choose a reuse license at submission: CC0, CC-BY, CC-BY-NC, CC-BY-ND, CC-BY-NC-ND, or 'no reuse without permission'.
No submission fee.
Screening typically completes within 2-4 days.
Revisions are intended for substantial updates (e.g. new datasets, expanded discussion), not minor edits.
Accepted submission formats in order of preference: (La)TeX/AMS(La)TeX/PDFLaTeX source (preferred), PDF, or HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
arXiv does not accept Word (.docx) documents directly; authors should save/export as PDF and submit that instead.

arXiv does not accept dvi, PostScript, or PDF that was produced from TeX/LaTeX source (submit the TeX source itself in that case); PDFs from TeX/LaTeX source are rejected unless a case-by-case exception is granted.
arXiv does not accept scanned documents in any format.
For a PDF submission: submit one single PDF file including all text and figures (no multiple PDFs or mixed file types).
PDF submissions must have all fonts embedded; use outline fonts (TrueType/Type1), not bitmap (Type3) fonts, and enable 'compatibility mode' when generating the PDF.
Bitmapped/scanned PDFs, OCR-converted PDFs, Type 3 fonts from TeX, and improperly exported fonts from Google Docs/Word all harm machine-readability and should be avoided.
Embedded JavaScript (e.g. animated content) in a submitted PDF causes automatic rejection; submit multimedia as separate ancillary files instead.
For TeX submissions: if multiple source files are used (chapters, appendices, etc.) package them as a .tar or .zip archive.

TeX submissions must include a .bib file or a pre-generated .bbl file if BibTeX/Biber is used; the .bbl filename must match the corresponding .tex filename, and for biblatex the .bbl must be produced by the same backend (Biber or BibTeX) used to compile the document.

If using makeindex, the .ind file must be included; if using glossary/nomenclature packages, the .gls or .nls files must be included -- these are exceptions to the general rule against including auxiliary/generated files.

All figures referenced via \includegraphics (or equivalent) must be included in the submission; arXiv performs no automatic figure format conversion, so figures must already be pre-converted to the correct format.
Exclude auxiliary/generated files such as .aux, .log, .toc, .lot, .lof, .dvi, .ps and output .pdf files, and any hidden files/directories (e.g. .cache/) -- these are deleted at announcement.
The psfig package is no longer supported; use graphicx instead. Custom publisher style files/macros not on TeX Live are not available.

Avoid the \today macro (causes periodic PDF rebuilds), avoid explicitly setting \pdfoutput or driver options for graphics/hyperref packages, and avoid double-spaced 'referee mode' output (submit single-spaced).
The xr package for cross-referencing external documents is generally problematic since links to external files will not work after processing.

arXiv auto-detects the correct TeX processor (and biblatex backend) in most cases during submission; compilation always occurs from the submission root directory even if main files are in subdirectories.
Only these characters are permitted in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , = ; file names are case-sensitive and must match exactly as referenced in LaTeX figure-inclusion commands.
Submissions with omitted figures are rejected even if an external link to the figures is provided.
Abstracts longer than 1920 characters will not be accepted.
Do not begin the abstract with the word 'Abstract'.
Only a limited set of TeX commands is supported in the abstract (rendered via MathJax); remove font commands such as \em or \it and spacing commands like ~, \,, or \ .
Avoid starting lines with whitespace unless intentionally preventing automatic line wrapping, and minimize unnecessary blank lines.
When the abstract is formatted for email announcement it is wrapped to 80 characters.
References to other arXiv articles in the abstract should use standard arXiv reference format to enable automatic linking.
Accepted figure format depends on the TeX compilation mode: plain TeX/LaTeX in DVI mode only supports .ps or .eps figures; LaTeX in PDF mode and PDFLaTeX support .pdf, .png, and .jpg.
Mixed figure formats within one submission can cause compilation failures.
Use standard macro packages (graphics, graphicx) to include figures.
Starting February 2026, arXiv will issue a warning during submission if an image exceeds 34 megapixels (about the size of a full-page A4 image at 600 dpi).
No automatic figure conversion is performed; figures must be pre-converted by the author to a supported format.
For an HTML-based submission, figures must be JPEG, PNG, or GIF.

Since February 2026 arXiv warns during submission about images larger than 34 megapixels (about a full A4 page at 600 dpi); oversized figures should be shrunk by format or resolution, with larger versions supplied as ancillary files or links.

arXiv has no editorial formatting rules (no mandated fonts, margins, line spacing, page limits, section structure, or required declarations/statements) -- its requirements are limited to file format, source/compilation rules, and the abstract character limit documented above.

The submit_docx.html help page returned HTTP 404 at retrieval time; guidance on Word documents was instead found via web search and consolidated into manuscript.notes (arXiv does not accept .docx directly).
Structured-abstract heading set and 150-word recommendation confirmed verbatim on the live author-guidelines page. Some flexibility on headings is allowed if authors feel them inappropriate.

Up to 7 pages formatted in the journal template, approx. 5,000 words excluding figures (Format-Free submission also uses this word count as the guide). Presents new research: models, algorithms, software involving new methods, biological databases and network information services. Actual biological data must be used; simulated data alone is accepted only in extremely well-justified cases.

Heading set confirmed verbatim on the live author-guidelines page; Summary should be one or two sentences. No explicit word cap stated for this shorter abstract beyond being 'much shorter' than the Original Paper abstract.
Up to 4 pages, approx. 2,600 words; alternatively approx. 2,000 words plus one figure.
Software, data, or network services described must be freely available to non-commercial users at the time of submission and maintained/available for at least two years following publication.
Web services must not require mandatory registration by the user; must not describe trivial utilities or tools requiring significant install effort. Software name should be in the title.
May be in a format best suited to subject matter, but should include a Title page, Structured Abstract, Text (sub-divided into sections), and References.

3-8 printed pages, approx. 3,000-6,000 words excluding figures. Most review papers are commissioned; prospective authors should first submit a one-page draft or summary to the editors for consideration.
No explicit page or word limit stated in the guidelines retrieved.
For discussion of technical, scientific, or broad topics related to bioinformatics and computational biology, including discussion of previously published papers.

Format-Free submission is offered: manuscripts can be submitted unformatted (into journal style only required at revision), provided they stay within the type's page/word guide; exceeding the limit by 20%+ risks immediate return by the editorial office without review.

Initial submissions: .doc/.rtf/.odf or PDF word-processing formats, or LaTeX source files submitted directly; LaTeX must use the OUP LaTeX template (Overleaf/CTAN/direct download), article style only, two-column text with 86mm column widths -- compile to PDF/PS before uploading since ScholarOne does not compile LaTeX.
For initial submission it is preferable to insert low-resolution figures/tables directly into the word-processing document, though they may alternatively be uploaded as separate files.

Revised manuscripts must be uploaded as a .doc/.rtf file with all tables, figures, schemes and equations inserted, or as complete LaTeX source with supporting files; changes should be marked with track changes or highlighting.
Journal follows Oxford SCIMED and CBE Style Manual (5th ed.) conventions; SI units preferred; genotypes italicized, phenotypes not italicized.
Mac users must include a three-letter file extension on every file (.doc, .rtf, .jpg, .gif, .tif, .ppt, .xls, .pdf, .eps, .mov); use simple file names, avoid special characters and spaces.
No page charges; no color charges (color figures are free).
Confirmed verbatim on the live author-guidelines page for Original Papers (150 words recommended, not a hard cap). Applications Notes use a shorter, differently-headed structure -- see article_types.
Internet hyperlinks in the abstract should be given as 'clickable text', e.g. {{http://www...}}.
Text abstracts must be written in English.
A data availability statement is a requirement for all papers published in the journal.
All authors must disclose any potential conflict of interest at the point of submission.
Author contributions should be described using the CRediT (Contributor Roles Taxonomy) framework.
Ethics-approval statements are required 'wherever appropriate', following international and local guidelines.

Use of LLMs must be explicitly declared and documented with sufficient detail in the supplementary materials; LLMs cannot be listed as authors; acceptable uses are limited to grammar/spell-checking, translation (author-verified), code-writing assistance, documentation, and finding inconsistencies -- drafting whole papers or peer-reviewing with an LLM is not permitted.

Funding details go in an 'Acknowledgements' section (Funding appears first within it): sentence must begin 'This work was supported by ...', full official funder name, grant numbers in brackets, multiple grants comma-separated, agencies separated by semicolons.
Original papers: Title page, Structured Abstract, Introduction, System and methods, Algorithm, Implementation, Discussion, References.
Reviews: Title page, Structured Abstract, Text (sub-divided into sections as suited to the subject matter), References.
Applications notes: Title page, Short Structured Abstract, Text.
Acknowledgements (including Funding as its first subheading) go at the end of the text, not in footnotes.
Publication-quality figures: 1200 dpi for line drawings, 350 dpi for colour/half-tone artwork; a second, low-resolution version (.jpg/.gif/.tif/.eps) is prepared for the review process.
All figures should be embedded within the text inside the main manuscript file and formatted to fit a single (86mm) or double (178mm) column width; figure legends appear adjacent to the figure.
Web screen dumps are discouraged in favor of tables/figures; figures should have a white background for contrast; colour figures are free of charge.
Alt text (alternative text) is required for all images/figures/illustrations/photographs in the main article, placed directly under the figure legend preceded by 'Alt text:'.

A graphical abstract is optional: single figure, landscape orientation, large enough text for social-media use, submitted as a separate file named 'graphical_abstract'; peer reviewed and appears in the TOC and search results.
Tables should be embedded within the main document file, numbered consecutively, self-explanatory with a brief descriptive title; footnotes indicated by lower-case letters.
All additional text, figures, and tables must be presented in a single file, submitted separately from the manuscript for review.
Accepts the same formats as the manuscript/figures; Excel spreadsheets and PowerPoint files are also accepted for supplementary material but will not be converted to PDF.

Machine-learning papers: the training-dataset/cross-validation/independent-test-set description required by the 'Machine learning' policy goes in the supplementary material for Application Notes (in the Methods section for Original Papers).

All publicly available datasets must be fully referenced in the reference list with an accession number or a unique identifier such as a DOI; recommended data-citation format: '[dataset] Authors, Year, Title, Publisher, Identifier'.

Previous work in the field should be cited; authors are responsible for reference accuracy. Personal communications and unpublished data should be cited sparingly and only when peripheral to the discussion; accepted-but-unpublished work is cited as 'in press'.
All submissions must be accompanied by a cover letter explaining the suitability of the paper for Bioinformatics; submissions omitting one may be editorially rejected.
If the manuscript deviates from the Instructions to Authors (e.g. a machine-learning paper departing from the stated requirements), the reasons must be explained in the cover letter.
The cover letter must also disclose and provide copies of all related/similar preprints, dissertations, manuscripts, and papers by the same authors, with an explanation of how the submission differs.
No explicit maximum per-file or total upload size was found in the guidelines retrieved.

Bioinformatics is fully open access (Creative Commons Attribution, CC BY, or the Open Government Licence for UK Crown-body content); corresponding authors must pay open-access charges or use an institutional Read and Publish agreement; discounts available for Low and Middle Income Country authors. No page charges; no color charges.
Single-anonymized peer review: author identities known to editors and reviewers, reviewers anonymous to authors; manuscripts typically sent to 3 reviewers.
ORCID iD is required for the submitting author at submission.

Manuscript category options confirmed via the live submission form: Applications note, Author Index, Editorial, Fast track, Genome Report, Letter to the Editor, Message from the ISCB, Original paper, Review (paperpush's article_type options -- Original Paper, Letter to the Editor, Applications Note, Review -- are a subset of these).

Software/database/web-server submissions: source code must be freely available at a stable URL (e.g. GitHub, Bitbucket) without a login requirement, and archived in a repository such as Zenodo, Figshare, Software Heritage, CRAN, or Bioconductor with a DOI; web servers must use HTTPS, be accessible without mandatory login, include test data and tutorials, and be supported/maintained for at least 3 years after publication. Submission to Code Ocean is encouraged for reproducibility.

Manuscripts using machine learning must include a dedicated subsection describing the composition of the training dataset, cross-validation, and independent test sets, address sequence homology between training/test sets for biological data, and report performance on an independent test set; leave-one-out validation will be editorially rejected unless there is a special circumstance.
Manuscripts are screened for plagiarism (iThenticate) and for inappropriate image manipulation / papermill activity.
Accepted manuscripts are published online as an Accepted Manuscript within about one week, ahead of copyediting into the Version of Record.

The journal accepts manuscript transfers from Briefings in Bioinformatics, Molecular Biology and Evolution, NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics, Nucleic Acids Research, and Systematic Biology; it also accepts direct submission from bioRxiv preprints.
No explicit page or word limit is stated in the Journal's guidelines (checked General_Instructions and Criteria_Scope); authors are encouraged toward concise, focused contributions.
No explicit page or word limit is stated; follows the same manuscript format and quality-review criteria as Standard Articles.

Must describe novel techniques, or highly significant advances in existing techniques, with utility/advantage to an extended (not purely specialist) audience, and must be the first report of that utility/application.
Requires comparative, benchmarked evidence of advantage over existing approaches using experimental (not simulated or reconstructed) data, proven effective at genome-wide scale.

Discourages: methods already published with prior applications, simple extensions/optimizations of mature existing technologies, comparative studies without significant novel conclusions, and step-by-step laboratory protocols (redirected to Biology Methods and Protocols).
A novel method may alternatively be reported within a Standard Article annotated with a '+M' designation, rather than as a dedicated Methods paper.

New submissions: typically 4-5 typeset journal pages. Update papers: typically no more than 4-6 journal pages (considered only 18+ months after the previous publication). Authors may request approval from the editor for a longer manuscript.

Submission to the Database Issue is by invitation only, after a pre-submission inquiry to the Executive Editor by 1 July; the deadline for new articles is 15 August (manuscripts not accepted before 1 June).
The database's homepage/landing page should not appear as a figure in the typeset article; a representative screenshot of query output is permissible instead.
For initial submission a single .pdf is acceptable; the manuscript text (incl. references, figure legends, simple tables) may otherwise be .doc, .rtf, or LaTeX.
Abstract and article text must include a valid URL through which the database can be accessed; database name should be the first word of the title where possible.
A graphical abstract is mandatory: minimum 5:2 aspect ratio, 127x50mm (or 5x2in), 300-600 dpi, landscape orientation, sans-serif font 12-16pt, .tif/.eps/editable .pdf.
Citations by sequential number only, in order of appearance in the text.
References must be in the correct journal format.
A valid URL through which the database can be accessed must be included in both the abstract and the article text.
The database must be completely functioning and available for review at the time of submission, and must remain available at the same URL for at least 5 years after the publication date.
Six suggested independent referees, with institutional affiliations and email addresses, are required (not recent collaborators, not from the same institution/city as any author).
All supplementary data must be available at the time of submission.
HTTPS is required where sensitive data are involved and encouraged otherwise; databases must be freely accessible without login/registration (narrow, documented exemptions apply).
4-5 printed journal pages; authors are urged to be succinct given the tight page constraints.

A one-page suitability summary (can be a PDF) must be sent to the editorial office before submission; the summary must include descriptions of input/output/processing method, PubMed IDs of prior related publications, and 2-4 keywords.
For initial submission a single .pdf is acceptable; the manuscript text may otherwise be .doc, .rtf, or LaTeX.
In addition to the abstract, the submission form requires a 'Key Points' box of up to three short bullet-point sentences summarizing key features.
A valid URL from which the software/server can be accessed must be included in the abstract.

A graphical abstract is mandatory (submitted as an additional file); the landing page of a web server should not be used as a figure unless necessary for explanation -- screenshots of results are preferred over homepage displays.
References must include active electronic DOI and PubMed Central links where available (a PubMed abstract link if no PMC link exists).
Required manuscript components: a software description (inputs, outputs, computation range), comparison with existing methods, and one or more use-case studies demonstrating biological insight.
The software must be completely functional and have been extensively tested at the time of submission.
Six suggested independent referees, with institutional affiliations and email addresses, are required.

A typical article occupies approximately 15 printed pages and includes 4-10 display items (figures/tables) and 100-150 references, although shorter, more focused contributions are also encouraged. Authors should have a strong publication record in the field.

Not a selectable option on the manuscript-category dropdown described in the Journal's General Instructions (Standard Article, Methods, Database Issue, Web Server Issue, Critical Reviews and Perspectives, Matters Arising); editorials are generally written or commissioned by the editorial team rather than externally submitted, and no author-facing formatting/length guidelines were found.
No specific formatting or length guidelines for this article type were found on the guideline pages retrieved, though it is a selectable manuscript category.
No explicit page or word limit found for Standard Articles; authors are encouraged to be concise.

For initial submission, authors are encouraged to submit a single .pdf file containing the main text, references, tables and figures, all embedded in the text to facilitate reviewing; supplementary data is uploaded as separate file(s).
Explicit 'Do': number all pages, embed TrueType fonts in Word documents, use single-column and single-spaced text (unless using LaTeX), submit a graphical abstract.
Explicit 'Don't': use line-numbering; use footnotes.
Revised manuscripts must be .docx/.rtf/LaTeX (not PDF), with tables/figures/captions embedded, submitted as both a tracked-changes ('red') copy and a clean copy.
Materials and Methods is placed before Results for ALL submission types (not just Standard Articles); essential experimental procedures must be in the main text, not relegated to supplementary files.
LaTeX users should use the OUP LaTeX template ('Modern Large' design, available on Overleaf); only the compiled PDF is required at initial submission, LaTeX source is requested at revision.
NAR partners with Cactus Communications to offer the Paperpal Preflight tool for pre-submission technical checks (optional).
Title must be clearly intelligible to a non-specialist; jargon and non-standard abbreviations are not permitted.
Author affiliations must include at minimum Department/Division/Unit, Institution, Town, Postal Code, Country.
Equal-contribution authors are marked with a dagger and a footnote; joint corresponding authors are marked with an asterisk.
Abstract must be a single paragraph not exceeding 200 words, written in English.

URLs, references to figures or schemes, reference citations, and non-standard abbreviations must NOT be included in the abstract -- except that Database Issue and Web Server Issue submissions MUST include a valid URL in the abstract.
Materials and Methods is placed before the Results section, for all submission types.

A list of essential Materials-and-Methods sub-headings is requested where relevant: Reagents, Biological Resources, Statistical Analyses, Novel Programs/Software/Algorithms, Web Sites/Data Base Referencing.
A 'Supplementary Data' statement ('Supplementary Data are available at NAR Online') is required whenever supplementary material is included.
A Data Availability statement is mandatory in all papers, placed at the end of the manuscript.
An Author Contributions statement is mandatory for all articles (preferably at original submission, no later than revision); CRediT taxonomy encouraged.
All authors must disclose potential conflicts of interest at submission; the corresponding author ensures all co-authors' conflicts are declared.
Funding-source disclosure (for the Open Access charge) is requested/encouraged but not compulsory; the Funding subheading follows Acknowledgements.

AI/LLM use (content/image generation, code, data processing, translation) must be disclosed both in the cover letter and in the Methods or Acknowledgements section; AI tools cannot be listed as authors and the Journal screens for them in author lists.
Human-subjects research requires ethics-committee/IRB approval (or documented exemption) and informed consent, per the Declaration of Helsinki; participant data must be anonymized.

Animal research requires institutional animal-care-committee approval and compliance with national/international guidelines (ARRIVE recommended); committee name and permit/license numbers must be in the Methods, with euthanasia/anesthesia and housing/husbandry details.

No NAR-specific dpi/format/dimension requirement is stated for ordinary in-text manuscript figures on the guideline pages retrieved; high-resolution images are required, preferably at initial submission but no later than revision.

Generic OUP-wide (not NAR-specific) figure-prep guidance: min 300 dpi colour half-tones, min 600 dpi greyscale half-tones, 600-900 dpi combination/line art, min 1200 dpi monochrome line art; RGB or CMYK; Arial/Times New Roman/Courier/Symbol fonts; text no smaller than 7pt at intended print size; line thickness 0.25-1pt. Treat as recommended defaults pending journal-specific confirmation, not a stated NAR rule.
All figures and captions should be embedded in the text (to facilitate reviewing); multipanel figures submitted as one composite image; figures numbered consecutively in citation order.

Graphical abstract is mandatory for ALL article types (not only Database/Web Server issues) at initial submission: 5:2 aspect ratio minimum, 127x50mm (or 5x2in) minimum, landscape orientation, sans-serif font (e.g. Arial) 12-16pt; submitted as a separate file named 'graphical_abstract'; must be original artwork (not a reused main/supplementary figure) and use colour.
Alt text is required for all images/figures/illustrations/photographs, included in the main manuscript file directly under each figure legend, preceded by 'Alt text:'.

Separate, optional 'cover figure' submissions (Database and Web Server issues only) have their own spec: .tif, min 300 dpi, CMYK, 220mm width x 165mm depth requiring no reduction/enlargement, no text/logos/labels.

Image manipulation rules: no feature may be enhanced/obscured/moved/removed/introduced; composite images (from different experiments/gels/blots) must show explicit dividing lines and be described in the legend; only whole-image brightness/contrast/colour adjustments that do not obscure information are allowed, and non-linear adjustments must be disclosed.
All tables and captions should be embedded in the text; if needed, individual tables should also be submitted in an editable format (Word, Excel, or PowerPoint), not as an image file.
Avoid colour/shading and tabbed spacing; provide a clear title, units in column/row headers (not the table body), and short descriptive captions (no interpretation).

Supplementary data must be uploaded as separate file(s) from the main article, preferably in PDF format at revision; must be referred to in the main manuscript at an appropriate point and is not typeset (published online as submitted).
No explicit supplementary file-size or file-count cap was stated on the pages retrieved.
Cited in the text by sequential number only, in order of appearance, and listed numerically in the References section.

Personal communications, unpublished results, manuscripts submitted/in preparation, statistical packages, computer programs and web sites are cited in the text only, NOT included in the reference list.
If there are four or more authors, list the first three followed by 'et al.'; full titles of journal articles must be provided; journal names abbreviated per Chemical Abstracts style.
Preprints are an allowed reference type (example format given for bioRxiv preprints).
Multiple references or page spans under one citation number are not allowed.

Not stated as mandatory for every fresh submission, but required content in specific cases: resubmissions must include a cover letter with the earlier manuscript number and full details of the previous version; the cover letter must disclose related/similar preprints, dissertations, manuscripts and papers by the same authors; it is where authors request excluded reviewers (with justification) and disclose AI/LLM use; it must give permission details for any third-party data cited as personal communication.
No explicit maximum per-file or total upload size was found on the guideline pages retrieved.
NAR is fully open access, published under CC BY, CC BY-NC, the US Government Open Licence, or the UK Open Government Licence; from 2025 NAR is published online only (24 issues/year).

Single-anonymized peer review: author identities known to editors and reviewers, reviewer identities hidden from authors. Standard/Methods/Critical Review submissions are typically sent to 2 reviewers.

Authors must suggest a minimum of six potential peer reviewers at submission (applies broadly, not just to the Database/Web Server issues); Database and Web Server issues additionally require specific referee criteria (not recent collaborators, not from the same institution/city).
ORCID iD is mandatory for the submitting author.

Software, databases, web servers, and datasets must be freely available over the internet without login/registration and maintained in fully functional form, ideally at the same URL, for a minimum of 5 years; code must be deposited to Zenodo or FigShare with a permanent DOI provided in the Data Availability statement at revision or acceptance.

Research materials (strains, clones, cell lines, hybridomas, genetically modified organisms) must be available to qualified investigators, freely or at reasonable cost, for at least 5 years from publication.
Manuscripts describing synthetic oligomers or nucleic-acid mimics for modulating gene expression must include a complete base-sequence description and details of the chemical modification pattern.

Revisions are encouraged within 30-60 days of decision, with extensions up to a total of 6 months available on request with justification; manuscripts are automatically withdrawn after 6 months without resubmission.
Preprints are permitted, including direct submission from bioRxiv to NAR; the preprint should be updated with the DOI of the published paper upon acceptance.

Manuscript categories confirmed via the live submission-category dropdown: Critical Reviews and Perspectives, Database Issue, Matters Arising, Methods, Standard Article, Web Server Issue (no separate 'Editorial' option was present in that dropdown).
Reviews generally run less than 7,000 words with 4 moderate display items; overall length is at the editor's discretion.
All Reviews start with a 200-word-maximum preface that sets the stage and ends with a summary sentence; the preface is also indexed on PubMed/Medline.
For the 5-10% most important references, provide a single bold sentence beneath the reference explaining its significance ('highlighted references').
As a guideline, most Reviews include no more than 150 references (exceptions possible).
Perspectives follow the same formatting guidelines as Reviews (up to ~7,000 words, 4 moderate display items, 200-word-maximum preface, highlighted references for the top 5-10% of citations).
Perspectives are more forward-looking/speculative than Reviews, may take a narrower field of view, and may be opinionated but should remain balanced.
Same guideline as Reviews: no more than 150 references.
Main text should be as concise as possible and ideally not exceed 1,200 words.
Contributions should start with a brief non-specialist summary paragraph, used as the abstract for submission purposes.
A simple message ideally requiring only one or two small figures/tables; complex figures/tables may be presented as Extended Data (ideally no more than three such items).
At submission, figures should be of sufficient quality for referees, ideally as JPEGs.
Only comments/clarifications on original research or peer-reviewed material published within the previous 18 months are eligible.

Called the 'Summary': a single paragraph of no more than 150 words, covering background/purpose, principal results and approaches/model systems, and major conclusions; should not include reference citations or non-standard abbreviations.

Manuscript must include a 'Resource Availability' section with 'Lead Contact', 'Materials Availability', and 'Data and Code Availability' subheadings.

Cell Systems is a figure-driven journal; the scientific argument should be made through the figures and their legends.

Resolution at intended print size: color/grayscale at least 300 dpi, black-and-white (non-line-art) at least 500 dpi, line art at least 1,000 dpi.
TIFF and PDF are the preferred production formats; EPS (vector), JPEG, and CDX are also accepted via Editorial Manager.

A graphical abstract is optional for Cell Systems (unlike most other Cell Press journals): square, 1200 x 1200 px at 300 dpi, single panel; preferred formats TIFF/PDF/JPG.
Figures with micrographs need a labeled scale bar; figures with pooled data/error bars must also define the measure (e.g., mean +/- SEM) and n in the legend.

Editable MS Word tables (not images); black and white only (small embedded color graphics OK); numbered Table 1, Table 2, etc.; no line breaks, merged cells, tabs, or shading; footnotes use lowercase superscript letters.

.csv/.txt is recommended for datasets and code (non-proprietary formats), labeled 'Data S1', etc.; supplemental tables exceeding 3 pages must be provided as standalone Excel files; individual standalone SI files must not exceed 500 MB.

Seen only by handling editors, never by reviewers.

Randomized controlled trials must be prospectively registered in a publicly accessible, ICMJE-compliant registry; standard reporting checklists (CONSORT, PRISMA, STROBE, MOOSE, STARD, RATS) are recommended where applicable.
'Authors' information' is an optional, non-canonical extra subsection and must not describe competing interests.

figures.font: Arial or Helvetica (Courier permitted for monospaced text); all fonts must be embedded
notes: Accepted formats: EPS, PDF, Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, TIFF, JPEG, PNG, BMP, CDX -- confirmed on the live general submission-guidelines page.
Individual figure files should not exceed 10 MB.

PDF page/figure width should be 85 mm for a half-page-width figure or 170 mm for a full-page-width figure; maximum height for figure + legend is 225 mm; resolution approximately 300 dpi at final size.
For web display, figures are shown at 600 pixels wide (standard) or 1200 pixels wide (high resolution).
Figure title (max 15 words) and legend (max 300 words) belong in the main manuscript, not the image file.
Figures numbered in citation order and uploaded in that order; multi-panel figures must be a single composite file.
Tables should not be embedded as images/figures or as spreadsheet files -- must use the word-processor Table object.
Table title (max 15 words) above the table; legend (max 300 words) underneath, outside table cells.
Color and shading may not be used in tables.
Tables under about one page can be embedded in the manuscript; larger tables should be placed as additional files instead.
Called 'Additional files' -- no formal distinction between the main article and supplementary material.
Maximum file size is 20 MB per additional file.
Each additional file must be cited sequentially in the main text and described with a file name, format (with extension), title, and description.
Tabular additional data should be provided as Excel spreadsheet (.xls/.xlsx) or CSV (.csv).
Only articles, clinical trial registration records, and abstracts that have been published or are in press (or are on a public preprint server) may be formally cited.
No overall reference-count limit is stated for Research, Software, Database or Review articles; Matters Arising has its own guideline (up to 15) -- see article_types.
Web links/URLs should be formatted as: title of the site, URL, and the date the site was accessed.

Must include: an explanation of why the manuscript should be published in BMC Bioinformatics; an explanation of any policy-related issues; a competing-interests declaration; confirmation that all authors have approved the manuscript for submission; a statement that the content has not been published elsewhere; the relevant special-issue/collection name if applicable.
Optionally may suggest peer reviewers (with institutional email addresses or ORCID identifiers) and/or reviewers to exclude.

BMC Bioinformatics's site has moved from bmcbioinformatics.biomedcentral.com to link.springer.com/journal/12859 (Springer Nature Link); the biomedcentral.com submission-guidelines URL still resolves to live content.

Confirmed article-type pages with dedicated formatting guidance: Research article, Database article, Software article, Review, Matters Arising. Valid article_type options in paperpush are comment, database, editorial, matters-arising, research, review, software -- 'comment' and 'editorial' have no dedicated guideline page (see their article_types notes); BMC Bioinformatics does NOT have separate 'Methodology' or 'Correspondence' article types the way sibling journal Genome Biology does.
The Article Processing Charge (APC) is £2290.00 GBP / $3090.00 USD / €2590.00 EUR (subject to a country-tiered pricing pilot); informational, not a submission-format requirement.
Single-anonymous peer review, consistent with the BMC-family template.

Research Articles should not exceed 3000 words of main text, plus an abstract, 3 to 5 display items (figures/tables) with brief legends, about 50 main-text references, and a structured acknowledgments section.

An extended online-only format is available for a few Research Articles: up to 6000 words, up to 6 display items (which may include videos), and up to 100 main-text references; the cover letter should explain why the extra length is merited.

Use single spacing (not double spacing) throughout the text, tables, and figure captions; format electronic files for US Letter (8.5 x 11 in) paper; use Times New Roman font and avoid Symbol fonts where possible.

For initial submission, upload a manuscript file (Word .docx preferred, prepared with AAAS's template) and, separately, a Combined PDF containing the full manuscript, figures, tables, and supplementary materials; both are required before proceeding.

LaTeX authors should convert to .docx if possible; otherwise use the AAAS LaTeX template (science_template.zip) and upload a compiled PDF for initial submission. Do not add \usepackage commands beyond those already in the template. Source files (.tex plus the generated .bbl) are required only at acceptance/production.
Materials and Methods are typically placed in the Supplementary Materials rather than the main text for Research Articles.
Titles should be no more than 96 characters, including spaces.

Unlike several sister journals (e.g. Science Translational Medicine, Science Immunology, Science Signaling), the flagship Science manuscript-assembly template has no 'One Sentence Summary' or short-title field.

Symbols (not superscripts) denote equal contribution, present address, and corresponding-author footnotes, in order: *, †, ‡, §, ¶, #, **, ††, ‡‡; * always marks the corresponding author. Co-first/co-senior author designations are not permitted; use the standard sentence 'These authors contributed equally to this work' instead.
Abstract should be 125 words or fewer, a single paragraph (no labelled subsections).
Content should flow as: a broad-audience background sentence, a more specific background sentence, objectives/methods, results, and a concluding sentence, in that order.
The template's 'Main Text' is a single section using free-form subheadings (up to 3 levels: bold, bold-italic, italic) rather than mandated Results/Discussion headers.
Acknowledgments are gathered into a paragraph after the final numbered reference.

The Acknowledgments paragraph covers, in order: non-author contributions, Funding, Author contributions (CRediT taxonomy encouraged, authors identified by initials), an optional Diversity/equity/ethics/inclusion statement, Competing interests, and Data/code/materials availability.
If all data are in the paper and supplementary materials, use the sentence 'All data are available in the manuscript or the supplementary materials.'

AI-assisted tools (LLMs, chatbots, image generators) cannot be listed as authors; any use must be disclosed (per the shared Science-family editorial policies), typically in the cover letter and in the methods or acknowledgments section.
Human-subjects research requires IRB (or equivalent) approval and a statement that informed consent was obtained; animal research requires a statement that care followed institutional/NIH guidelines.
Diversity, equity, ethics, and inclusion statements are optional and are not used as acceptance/rejection criteria.

figures.multipanel_labels: uppercase bold (A, B, C), 10 pt, upper-left corner
notes: Figures should be saved at 300 dpi for initial submission; a higher resolution applies at the revision stage.
Printed figure widths: 5.7 cm / 2.24 in (1 column), 12.1 cm / 4.76 in (2 columns), or 18.4 cm / 7.24 in (3 columns); symbol/lettering size about 7 pt (2.5 mm), not smaller than 5 pt.
PowerPoint files are not accepted; files must be readable by Adobe Photoshop or Illustrator; vector formats (e.g. Illustrator) are preferred for line art.

Digital enhancement/manipulation of images is restricted: linear contrast/brightness/color adjustment must be applied to an entire image or plate equally; nonlinear adjustments must be disclosed in the caption.
Color images in print cost $650 for the first color figure and $450 for each additional one.
Tables are included after the references; every column needs a heading with the unit of measure in parentheses; units should not change within a column.
Supplementary Materials are submitted as a single .docx and/or PDF file (max 50 MB), separate from the main text.

Auxiliary Supplementary Materials (large multimedia/data that don't fit the combined SM file): up to 10 files, 25 MB total; Movies are capped at 50 MB each, .mp4 preferred (.mov with h.264 also accepted; animated GIFs not accepted).
Tabulated data underlying figures should be uploaded as an additional 'data S1' file in a machine-readable format (csv, tsv, json, or xml).
Reference numbering in Supplementary Materials continues from the main text; references cited only in SM are suppressed in print and in the main-paper PDF.

references.style: Science style (numbered by order of citation, cited in text as italicized parenthetical numbers)
notes: References and Notes are numbered in the order cited: main text, then text boxes, then figure/table captions, then notes/acknowledgments, then Supplementary Materials.
All authors must be listed in each reference; 'et al.' is not permitted in place of the complete author list; op. cit. and ibid. are also disallowed.

About 50 main-text references is the guideline for standard Research Articles (up to 100 for the extended online-only format); citation of unpublished data or personal communications is not allowed to support conclusions, though preprints (arXiv, bioRxiv, etc.) may be cited.

Should include: the paper's title and a statement of its main point; information needed for a fair review, including related manuscripts submitted elsewhere; reference to any pre-submission discussions with editors; names of colleagues who saw the paper before submission; a statement that the material is not published or under consideration elsewhere; informed-consent and animal-care statements where applicable; and where the underlying data are or will be available.
Ideally 1 to 3 authors (no more than 7 without editor permission); less than 20% of the reference list should be the authors' own work; cannot contain analysis of unpublished data.

Presents original analysis of already-published data (formal meta-analyses count as original research, not Analytical Review); ideally no more than 7 authors; fewer than 20% of references should be the authors' own work.
2000 to 3000 words, 1 or 2 figures, up to 15 references; presents new, unpublished data/analyses on science-and-society policy issues.
2000 to 3000 words, 1 or 2 figures, up to 15 references; draws on already-published work rather than presenting new data.

Solicited Perspectives tied to a same-issue paper run ~1000 words; stand-alone (invited) Perspectives run ~1800 words; both are capped at 15 references and 1 figure or table, with no more than two authors.
Commentary on new books, films, exhibitions, performances, apps, podcasts, or other media of broad interest.
Discusses material published in Science within the past 3 months, or issues related to recent events of general interest; subject to editing for clarity and space.
Signed opinion piece, up to 2 authors; with rare exceptions solicited by the editors.
'Research Resource' is not a distinct submittable article type at flagship Science (unlike Science Advances and Science Signaling).

Most Commentary-section formats (Perspectives, Book/Media Reviews, Policy Forums, Editorials, Expert Voices) are largely editor-commissioned, though unsolicited Letters, Book/Media Reviews, and stand-alone Perspectives are accepted; eLetters are brief post-publication online comments, not a submittable manuscript type.

Authors submitting to Science may request transfer to a sister AAAS journal (Science Advances, Science Immunology, Science Robotics, Science Signaling, Science Translational Medicine) if not selected for publication at Science, without needing to reformat.
Reviews are limited to 10,000 words, up to 10 figures and/or tables (combined), and no more than 150 references (more may be permitted upon request).
Generally solicited by the editors, though unsolicited/complete reviews may also be considered (longer editorial-evaluation timeframe).

Presents a validated technique, tool, or informational database without the substantial analysis needed for a new research insight; follows the same format as a Research Article (the Results heading may be omitted if appropriate) and the same review process.
The Science Advances deputy editors decide whether to publish an article under the Research Resource tag.
Research Articles allow a flexible short-or-long format, up to 15,000 words, with up to 10 figures and/or tables (combined) and up to 80 references.

Initial submission has no required format/order beyond logical organization; it is uploaded as a single .docx file (or LaTeX plus PDF and supporting files) containing all components in sequence (title, main text, references, table/figure legends, then the Supplementary Materials list if applicable).
Tables and figures should be embedded in the text at first mention, with legends.
For best results use a universal font such as Times New Roman, since special fonts may affect figure/table rendering.
Should the manuscript be reviewed and revised, specific formatting may be required at that time; see 'Revised Manuscripts' and the topical-area style checklist.
Manuscript title: 135-character maximum. Short title: 50-character maximum.
An ORCID iD is required for the first and corresponding authors (not all authors) and strongly encouraged for the rest; each author must link their own ORCID account.
No 'one-sentence summary' or teaser field is listed on the Science Advances information-for-authors page.
Abstract: no more than 150 words, a single paragraph written for a general readership; graphic representations of the abstract are not permitted.
Content should flow as: a general-introduction sentence, a more specific background sentence, a brief objectives/methods statement, key results, and a concluding sentence.
Any abbreviation that appears in the title must be defined in the abstract.
Journal's own heading is 'Materials and Methods'; the Discussion section must include a paragraph on the study's limitations.

Acknowledgments (immediately after References) must include complete funding information, each author's contribution (by initials), a competing-interests statement, and a data/materials-availability statement.
Standard competing-interests sentence when none exist: 'The authors declare that they have no competing interests.'
Standard data-availability sentence: 'All data needed to evaluate the conclusions in the paper are present in the paper and/or the Supplementary Materials.'
Standard no-funding sentence: 'The authors acknowledge that they received no funding in support for this research.'

Digital enhancement/manipulation of images (including micrographs and gels) is not allowed; linear contrast/brightness/color adjustments must be applied to an entire image or plate equally; nonlinear adjustments must be disclosed in the legend.
Cover-image specs (for accepted manuscripts only): 2476 x 3137 px for a cover, 1280 x 427 px for a site image.

Detailed figure dpi/width specifications are in the separate AAAS 'Guide to Preparing Figures' linked from the Revised Manuscripts section; the Science-family defaults (300 dpi raster, vector line art) apply.
Table legend/units must be clearly legible and no more than 250 words; boldfaced label and title (e.g. 'Table 1. Findings.'); no footnotes in column heads.
Large datasets should go to Supplementary Materials rather than in-text tables.
Supplementary text, figures, and tables must be compiled into a single PDF (max 25 MB), both at initial submission and at revision; single-spaced.
Auxiliary Supplementary Materials/Movies (large multimedia or data that doesn't fit the combined PDF) are limited to 10 files combined, 25 MB total.
Supplementary figures/tables are cited in-text in lowercase (e.g. 'fig. S1', 'table S1'); Supplementary Materials are peer-reviewed along with the main text.

references.style: Science family (numbered, cited as parenthetical numbers)
notes: Up to 80 references for a standard Research Article (150 for a Review).
References are combined into a single list (main text plus Supplementary Material) numbered in order of first citation; footnotes/endnotes are not allowed.
Initial submissions may include 'in-press' references, but they must convert to 'published' before publication or be removed; personal communications and working papers are not acceptable references.

Must include: the article title; why the work is appropriate for Science Advances (what is new, how it advances the field); information needed for a fair review, including related manuscripts submitted elsewhere; a statement the material is not published or under consideration elsewhere; a competing-interests statement; informed-consent/animal-care statements where applicable; where the underlying data are or will be available; and a suggested Deputy/Section Editor and Associate Editor.
If the manuscript was previously posted as a preprint, disclosing the preprint DOI is standard practice under the shared Science-family editorial policies.

Science Advances is AAAS's open-access, online-only, interdisciplinary sister journal to Science; unlike the print-constrained flagship, it has no page limit and a substantially higher reference allowance (80 vs. ~50 for a standard Research Article).

Article types confirmed on the information-for-authors page: Research Article (default, used at top level), Research Resource, Review; Focus articles and Editorials exist but are commissioned only by the Editorial Board (not open to unsolicited submission, so not modeled here).
Authors must submit five potential reviewers (name, affiliation, email) and may exclude up to three.
Up to 8000 words (including abstract, main text, references, and figure legends); short pithy title; abstract of no more than 75 words; up to 4 figures/tables (with legends).
Less than 1000 words; no abstract; references kept to a minimum, no more than 5; no figures or tables (aside from an author photo).

Cannot exceed 1800 words total, including abstract, main text, references, and figure legend; short snappy/newsy title; one-sentence abstract; no more than 10 references; one figure (with legend) or table.

Should not exceed 2500 words total, including abstract, main text, references, and figure legends; short pithy title; abstract of 50 words or fewer; no more than 15 to 20 recent references; 1 or 2 figures (with legends) or tables.

Less than 1000 words, no more than 10 references, may have one figure or table; responds to an article published in Science Immunology within the previous two months, or raises issues of interest to the immunology community.

Research Articles should be 6000 to 8000 words in length with 5 to 8 figures; word count is not explicitly stated to exclude the abstract/references/legends on the initial-submission page (unlike some sister journals' 'not including X' phrasing).
Preferred single complete .docx file (Word 2007/2010 for PC, Word 2008/2011 for Mac) containing all figures and tables; use of the Word template facilitates automatic metadata extraction.
Shorter Research Articles with fewer figures may be published as Reports at the editors' discretion.

Required sections: Abstract, Introduction, Results, Discussion, Materials and Methods, References and Notes; the Materials and Methods section must include a 'Study Design' subsection (and a 'Statistical Analysis' subsection) per the Design and Statistics Guidelines.
Titles should be no more than 135 characters, including spaces (confirmed on the Research-Article initial-submission page; this supersedes any lower figure seen elsewhere).
A one-sentence summary capturing the paper's most important point is required for all papers; no character limit is stated for Science Immunology (unlike Science Robotics' 125-character cap).
Symbols, abbreviations, and acronyms must be defined at first use except in the title, one-sentence summary, and Abstract.
Preferred length is 125 words or fewer; 250 words is the stated maximum allowed for submission.
Should present background to convey context, a general idea of methodology, describe results, and draw general conclusions about the clinical implications of the work for a general reader.
Full assembly order: Abstract, Introduction, Results, Discussion, Materials and Methods, References and Notes, Figures and Tables, Supplementary Materials.

Acknowledgments (gathered into a paragraph after the final reference) must include complete funding information, each author's contribution, a listing of any competing interests (all authors also complete a Conflict of Interest form), and a data/materials-availability statement with accession numbers for any public-database deposits.
Informed consent must be obtained for human research (and stated in the manuscript), with IRB/equivalent approval; editors may request IRB documentation.

Clinical trials should follow the CONSORT Statement (checklist + participant flow diagram at submission) and be registered per ICMJE criteria, with the registration number in Acknowledgments and cited as a reference.
For initial submission, high resolution is not required (lower-resolution figures are acceptable to reduce file size); high-resolution/vector files are needed only if a revision is invited.
Electronic figures should be sized to fit on single 8.5x11-in or A4 paper, preferably at 1 (3.5 in), 1.5 (5.0 in), or 2 (7.3 in) columns wide.
Symbol size minimum 6 pt, line width minimum 0.5 pt at final reduced size; avoid red/green together and grayscale for accessibility.

Supplementary Materials are submitted as a single separate file (.docx or PDF), max 25 MB, containing figures with captions and tables with captions; large multimedia/data files that don't fit go to Auxiliary Supplementary Materials (up to 10 files, 25 MB combined).
References cited only in Supplementary Materials are folded into the single main reference list, numbered continuing from the main text.
Video files: .mp4 preferred (.mov with h.264 acceptable), HD (1920x1080) where possible, animated GIFs not accepted; audio: .wav/.aiff/.au/.m4a preferred, min 160 kb/s bit rate.
References and Notes are numbered in the order first cited: main text, then figure/table legends, then Supplementary Materials; each reference appears only once, with a unique number.
Each reference must list all authors in full (no 'et al.'), plus the full article title, journal title, volume, year, and inclusive pagination.
No stated maximum reference count for Research Articles; per-article-type caps: Editorial 5, Focus 10, Letter 10, Perspective ~15-20, Review 100 (see article_types).

Should include: reference to any pre-submission discussions with editors; the paper's title and a statement of its main point; information needed for a fair review, including related manuscripts submitted elsewhere; names of colleagues who reviewed the paper; a statement that none of the material has been published or is under consideration elsewhere, including the Internet; informed-consent/animal-care statements where applicable; and where the data are or will be available.
A .docx version of the cover letter is required in addition to any other format.
Science Immunology accepts original Research Articles plus Reviews, Editorials, Focus articles, Perspectives, and Letters; Reviews, Editorials, and Focus articles are largely editor-commissioned.

Shared Science-family conventions (data/code/materials availability, competing interests, AI-use disclosure, preprint policy, human/animal research standards) are set out on the 'Science Journals: Editorial Policies' page rather than restated on the Science-Immunology-specific pages.
Reviewers: name, affiliation, and email required for up to five suggested and up to five excluded reviewers.
Currently invitation-only. Text, figure/table captions, references, and tables must all be in one .docx file.
Editor-invited Focus articles limit authorship to those invited, plus a maximum of one additional co-author.
Requires a one-sentence abstract, not a full structured abstract.
Up to one figure or table (with caption) allowed.
Title should be short, snappy, or newsy (no character limit stated, unlike Research Articles).
Currently invitation-only (presubmission inquiry required). A longer version may be considered at the Editor's discretion.
Short, pithy title required (no character limit stated).
Currently invitation-only (presubmission inquiry required). A longer version may be considered at the Editor's discretion. Sent for peer review.
Short, pithy title required (no character limit stated).
Forward-looking articles on key robotics research findings and outstanding challenges.
Research Article word limit (8000 words) excludes References only; abstract, methods, and figure legends are counted.
8 is a combined cap across figures, tables, and/or movies in the main text, not 8 figures alone.
Required sections: Abstract, Introduction, Results, Discussion, Materials and Methods, References, Figures and Tables, Supplementary Materials.
Preferred single .docx (Word 2007/2010 or 2008/2011 for Mac) file containing text, figures, and tables together; LaTeX users should convert to .docx or use the AAAS LaTeX template.
Authors must supply both a full title (max 100 characters) and a short title (max 40 characters).
One-sentence summary required for all Research Articles, max 125 characters and spaces.
Author list is one single paragraph, no line breaks; authors listed by first name/initial, middle initial, last name.
Single paragraph, not to exceed 250 words and ideally closer to 200, written in plain language for a general reader.
Must include an opening sentence stating the question/problem, background context, a brief statement of primary results, and a short concluding sentence.
No citations or undefined abbreviations; any abbreviation in the title must be defined in the abstract.
Full prescribed order also includes Figures and Tables, then Supplementary Materials, after References.
All authors must additionally complete a separate Conflict of Interest form (not just an in-text statement).
Data/code/materials availability statement must give the location of data not included in the paper, including accession numbers for any deposited data.

notes: Electronic figures should be sized to fit on single 8.5x11-in or A4 paper, preferably at 3.5, 5.0, or 7.3 inches wide (1, 1.5, or 2 columns).

To keep file sizes small, save figures at 300 dpi for initial submission; higher resolution and a different set of acceptable formats apply for revised figures after peer review. PowerPoint files are not accepted.
Symbol size minimum 6 pt, line widths minimum 0.5 pt for legibility when reduced.
Panels should be set close together; common axis labels should not be repeated.
Main manuscript file and the Supplementary Materials file each have a 25 MB size limit.

Large multimedia/data files that do not fit in the main supplementary file go in up to 10 auxiliary supplementary files, 25 MB combined; tabulated data underlying figures should be uploaded as an additional 'data S1' file in a machine-readable format (csv, tsv, json, or xml).
Supplementary videos must be .mp4 (preferred) or .mov with H.264 compression; HD frame size (1920x1080 px) preferred; animated GIFs are not accepted.

references.style: numbered, cited in order (through main text, then through figure/table captions)
notes: Each reference must list every author (no 'et al.'), the full article title, journal title/abbreviation, volume, year, and first and last page.
No explicit reference-count cap stated for Research Articles (unlike Focus/Review/Viewpoint, which do have caps).

Preferably .docx format. Must state the paper's title and its main point; disclose related manuscripts submitted elsewhere and name colleagues who reviewed the paper; include a statement that none of the material has been published or is under consideration elsewhere, including on the Internet; and give informed-consent/animal-care statements where applicable and where the data are/will be available.
Reviewers: name, affiliation, and email required for up to five suggested and up to five excluded reviewers.

Science Robotics states it follows the general Science-family manuscript style; shared conventions (double spacing, US Letter page size, data/code/materials availability, AI-use disclosure, preprint policy) come from the shared 'Science Journals: Editorial Policies' page rather than being restated with Robotics-specific text.

Science Robotics' own limits: 8000-word Research Article limit (excluding References), up to 8 combined figures/tables/movies, 250-word abstract cap (200 preferred), 100/40-character title limits, 125-character one-sentence summary, and the Focus/Review/Viewpoint word/reference/figure caps.

Research Resources and Reviews/Viewpoints are currently by invitation of the Editor only (presubmission inquiry required); Focus articles are also editor-commissioned. eLetters (brief online comments) are accepted but Science Robotics does not publish standalone Letters as a submittable article type.
Submission portal: Science Manuscript Submission & Information Portal (cts.sciencemag.org).
Non-hypothesis-driven research: validated new methods/tools or validated signaling-relevant data sets, selected from Research Article submissions.
Follows the same manuscript format and review process (editor evaluation, Board of Reviewing Editor evaluation, in-depth peer review) as a Research Article.
Online publishing has removed the need for strict word limits, but 8000 words is the guideline upper limit; precise length is dictated by the topic. Requires at least 2 figures or tables.
Preferred length is 125 words or fewer; 250-word maximum, same as Research Articles.
Structure: Abstract, Introduction, topical subsections, Conclusions, References and Notes.
At most 10 references; one of the 10 must be the highlighted research article the Focus discusses.
Always solicited by the editors; short, lively article featuring the author's opinion on a same-issue Science Signaling paper (or occasionally another topic).

It is not necessary to reformat manuscripts to Science Signaling style for initial submission; no explicit main-text word limit is stated on the Research-Article initial-submission page (unlike sister journals such as Science, Science Immunology, and Science Translational Medicine).
Required sections: Abstract, Introduction, Results, Discussion, Materials and Methods, References and Notes.
Use the past tense to describe the manuscript's own results and the present tense to describe previously published results.
Symbols, abbreviations, and acronyms must be defined at first use except in the title, one-sentence summary, and Abstract.
All content is submitted online via the AAAS/Science submission portal (cts.sciencemag.org).
Title may not exceed 135 characters including spaces; commonly used abbreviations need not be defined in the title.
A one-sentence summary capturing the paper's most important point is required; no character limit is stated for Science Signaling.
Title and author list with affiliations appear on the opening page of the single manuscript file (not a separate title-page file).
250 words is the stated maximum; abstracts of about 200 words are preferred.

Should explain to a general (non-specialist) reader why the research was done and why the results are important; must not state what is unknown/unclear or not previously investigated. No references or paragraph breaks are allowed in the Abstract.
Venue wording is 'Materials and Methods' and 'References and Notes'; mapped here to canonical Methods/References ids.

Only one additional level of subheadings is allowed (no third-level subheadings); a separate Materials and Methods section in Supplementary Materials is allowed only for computational, structural, or synthesis methodology, at the editor's discretion.
The paragraph following the last reference must contain, in order: Acknowledgments, Funding, Author Contributions, Competing Interests, Data and materials availability.
Author Contributions must refer to each author by initials (spell out last names if two authors share initials).
If there are no competing interests, use the exact statement: 'The authors declare that they have no competing interests.'

Data and materials availability must name the repository/identifier for any deposited data or code, and include the sentence 'All other [or 'All'] data needed to evaluate the conclusions in the paper are present in the paper or the Supplementary Materials.'

For initial submission, main figures should be at high resolution: 300-600 dpi for grayscale/color (halftone) images and 1200 dpi for line art. Embedded figures must have a minimum resolution of 300 dpi and must not be up-sampled.
Figures should be sized to one of four widths: 3.5, 5.0, 6.125, or 7.3 inches (88.9, 127.0, 155.6, or 185.4 mm); use the smallest that keeps the figure legible. Multi-page figures are not allowed.
It is not necessary to reformat figures to Science Signaling style for the initial submission; professional illustrators can help finalize figures after the paper is reviewed.

Supplementary figures and tables (with legends) are uploaded as a single Word (.docx) file, not PowerPoint or PDF, at initial submission; the inserted-figure resolution in this file should be 300-600 dpi.
Supplementary Material should be limited to information not essential for general understanding of the research presented in the main text.
Every Supplementary Materials item and every panel of a Supplementary figure must be cited at least once in the main manuscript.
References are numbered in the order first cited, through the text and then through figure/table legends, then Supplementary Materials; each reference has a unique number (no combined references).
No explicit maximum reference count stated for Research Articles; Focus is capped at 10.

Must include the manuscript title, a statement of the paper's main point, any information needed to ensure a fair review, reference to any pre-submission discussions with editors, and a statement that none of the material has been published or is under consideration elsewhere.
Authors wishing their submission to be considered as a Research Resource should say so in the cover letter.

Science Signaling publishes original Research Articles, Research Resources, Focus articles, and Reviews; most Focus articles and Reviews are solicited by the editors, though unsolicited complete manuscripts are also accepted for review.
Science Signaling no longer publishes Viewpoints or Protocols.

Shared conventions (double spacing, US Letter, data/code/materials availability, AI-use disclosure, preprint policy) come from the general 'Instructions for preparing an initial manuscript' and 'Science Journals: Editorial Policies' pages shared across the Science family rather than being restated on Signaling-specific pages.
The Science Signaling Editors do not accept presubmission inquiries for research papers, Focuses, or Reviews; complete manuscripts are submitted directly through cts.sciencemag.org.

Non-hypothesis-driven research presenting new validated methods/techniques or validated databases/data sets of direct relevance to translational medicine, providing at least some new biological insight; same format as a Research Article.
Short, pithy abstract of 100 words or less.
Short pithy title; up to four figures (with figure legends) or tables. Identifies specific challenges/bottlenecks preventing translation into clinical treatments, with suggestions to overcome them.
Short pithy title; 1 or 2 figures (with figure legends) or tables; sent for peer review. Analyzes recent key translational research from biomedical and clinical perspectives.
One-sentence abstract only.
Includes the paper under discussion in the count of 10.
Short newsy title; one figure (with figure legend) or one table; may be sent for peer review.
