References kept to a minimum, no more than 5.
Applies to the Research Article type, the journal's primary/default article type.
10,000-word limit is total, including main text, materials and methods, references, and figure legends.
Up to 8 figures in the main text.

Required sections: Abstract, Introduction, Results, Discussion, Materials and Methods, References and Notes; Materials and Methods must include an 'Experimental Design' subsection at the start and a 'Statistical Analysis' subsection at the end.
Shorter Research Articles with fewer figures may be published as Reports at the editors' discretion.
Title may not exceed 135 characters, including spaces.
A one-sentence summary capturing the paper's most important point is required for all papers; no character limit is stated.
No separate title-page file is used; the title, one-sentence summary, and author list appear on the first page of the single manuscript .docx.
Preferred length is 125 words or fewer; 250 words is the stated maximum for submission.
Should present background to convey context, a general idea of methodology, describe results, and draw general conclusions about the clinical implications; single unstructured paragraph.
Journal's own section name is 'Materials and Methods', mapped here to canonical 'Methods'.
Full file structure also includes Figures/Figure Legends, Tables/Table Legends, and (if present) Supplementary Materials, after References.

Acknowledgments (gathered into a paragraph after the final reference) include funding, each author's contribution, competing interests (all authors also complete a Conflict of Interest form), and data/materials availability with accession numbers for deposited data.
Clinical trial registration follows ICMJE criteria; provide the registration number in Acknowledgments and a link cited as a reference.
Informed consent must be obtained for human research (stated in the manuscript) with IRB/equivalent approval; editors may request IRB documentation.
All papers require a materials availability statement even when no new materials were created.

For initial submission, lower-resolution figures are acceptable to keep file sizes small; no specific dpi minimum is stated for initial submission (higher-resolution/vector files are required only if a revision is invited).
Electronic figures should be sized to fit on single 8.5x11-in or A4 paper, preferably at 1 (3.5 in), 1.5 (5.0 in), or 2 (7.3 in) columns wide.
Multipanel labels: capital letters (A, B, C...), 9 pt bold, placed at the upper-left of each panel.

Digital enhancement/manipulation of images is restricted: linear contrast/brightness/color adjustment must apply to an entire image or plate equally; nonlinear adjustments must be disclosed in the legend.

Supplementary Materials are optional; if included, prepared as a separate Word .docx file (PDF also accepted for initial submission) with embedded supplementary figures/captions and tables; not essential to the general understanding of the main text.
Auxiliary supplementary materials/data files not fitting the main file are uploaded separately per the shared Science-family conventions (up to 10 files, 25 MB combined; movies up to 50 MB each).
Supplementary text, figures, and tables go in a single combined file, as across the Science family.
References and Notes are numbered in the order first cited: main text, then figure/table legends, then Supplementary Materials.
Each citation must list all authors (no 'et al.'), the full article title, journal title, volume, year, and first and last page.
No explicit maximum reference count for the default Research Article; per-type caps: Review 100, Viewpoint 30, Focus 10, Editorial 5 (see article_types).

Should establish the 'translational bridge' (mechanistic finding plus human-facing relevance), explain fit with the journal, and include standard declarations: not under simultaneous submission elsewhere, informed-consent/animal-care statements where applicable, competing interests and funding disclosed, and data/materials availability confirmed.

Science Translational Medicine publishes Research Articles (and Research Resources, same format) plus Reviews, Editorials, Focus articles, and Viewpoints; Reviews/Editorials/Focus/Viewpoints are largely editor-commissioned or invited.

Shared conventions (double spacing, US Letter, data/code/materials availability, AI-use disclosure, preprint policy, clinical-trial/human-subjects standards) come from the shared 'Science Journals: Editorial Policies' page rather than being restated on STM-specific pages.
Submission portal: Science Manuscript Submission & Information Portal (cts.sciencemag.org).
Main text must be 9 pages or fewer at submission; strictly enforced, papers over the limit are desk-rejected.
Page limit increases to 10 pages for the discussion/rebuttal phase and for camera-ready, to allow new results/discussion.
References do not count toward the page limit and unlimited additional pages are allowed for the bibliography.
Authors may use as many pages of appendices (placed after the bibliography) as they wish; reviewers are not required to read the appendix.

Submission is via OpenReview (https://openreview.net/group?id=ICLR.cc/2027/Conference); only 'Abstract' is mandatory at the abstract-deadline stage, full PDF can be uploaded any time before the paper deadline.
The style-file bundle iclr-2027-style-files.zip contains iclr2027_conference.sty, iclr2027_conference.bst, and the iclr2027_conference.tex template.
AI use statement is required; see the AI Policy for Authors (https://iclr.cc/Conferences/2027/AIPolicyForAuthors). Does not count toward the page limit.

Ethics statement is recommended (not required for all submissions), placed at the end of the main text before references; should be no more than 1 page; does not count toward the page limit. Only needed if the paper raises potential Code of Ethics concerns (human subjects, sensitive datasets, dual-use research, conflicts of interest, bias/fairness, privacy, legal compliance, research integrity).

Reproducibility statement is recommended, a paragraph at the end of the main text before references, pointing to where reproducibility-supporting material lives (code, proofs, data processing description) rather than restating it; does not count toward the page limit.
All authors must read and explicitly acknowledge the ICLR Code of Ethics and Code of Conduct during submission.
Authors are encouraged (not required) to submit a single file containing paper + supplementary text; supplementary text should appear after the references and be clearly marked (e.g. as an appendix).
Source code can be uploaded as supplementary material (e.g. anonymized code in a .zip) or linked via an anonymous repository; encouraged but optional.
No supplementary file size cap is stated in the guidelines text.
Supplementary materials are due on the same deadline as the full paper.
No author may appear as a co-author on more than 20 submissions.
Each author may appear on at most one submission in which no author is a qualified reciprocal reviewer (i.e. authors new to major ML venues are capped at 1 ICLR 2027 submission).

Qualified reciprocal reviewer = has at least one accepted paper (primary conference track, not workshops/findings-adjacent types like tiny papers/blog posts/demos) at ICLR/NeurIPS/ICML/UAI/AISTATS/JMLR/TMLR, ACL/EMNLP/EACL/NAACL/IJCNLP-AACL/CL/TACL, COLM, CVPR/ICCV/ECCV/PAMI/3DV, AAAI/IJCAI/JAIR, ICRA/IROS/RSS/CoRL, KDD, or COLT, accepted by the abstract deadline.
All authors on 3+ papers must serve as a reviewer for at least 6 papers, or risk desk rejection of their submission(s) for incomplete/low-quality reviews.
Every submission must have at least one author registered to review at least 3 papers and qualified as above; if none of the authors register, the paper is desk-rejected.
Double-blind: papers must be anonymous; any identity leak in main text or supplementary material causes desk rejection. Citing the authors' own related arXiv work is allowed if cited in third person.

Dual submission of identical/substantially similar work under review elsewhere is not allowed; arXiv preprints and non-archival workshop presentations do not violate this policy; arXiv posting during review is allowed.
Submissions from entities/individuals subject to US sanctions (per the OFAC SDN list) will be desk-rejected, since ICLR is incorporated in the US.
All authors become de-anonymized at the end of the review process (including withdrawn papers, which are de-anonymized immediately on withdrawal after the submission deadline).
Every submitter (and all co-authors) must have an OpenReview profile; new non-institutional-email profiles can take up to two weeks to moderate.

Key 2026->2027 deadlines referenced during retrieval: abstract deadline Sep 18, 2026 11:59 PM AOE; full paper deadline Sep 25, 2026 11:59 PM AOE; reviews released Nov 05, 2026; public discussion Nov 05-18, 2026; decisions Dec 16, 2026 -- these are time-sensitive and should be re-verified close to the actual submission date.
This entry is based on the live ICLR 2027 AuthorGuidelines/CallForPapers pages (not the 2026 fallback), since the 2027 pages were complete and accessible at retrieval time.
Full-length original research article of more than 7 journal (typeset) pages, roughly 10+ full pages of a typical double-spaced manuscript. No stated upper limit.
Short, self-contained original research article of at most 7 journal (typeset) pages, roughly 10 full manuscript pages. Notes are processed on an expedited basis.

Under Elsevier's 'Your Paper Your Way' policy, submission proceeds fully online; the system converts source files to a single PDF used for peer review. Initial submission may be a single manuscript file (PDF, Word, etc.) -- separate source files are not required until revision or final submission.
LaTeX submissions are recommended to use the elsarticle.cls class and BibTeX for the bibliography; a dedicated LaTeX site provides templates and detailed instructions.

This journal uses a single anonymized peer review process: reviewer identity is not disclosed to authors. Submissions are first assessed by the editor for suitability, then typically sent to at least one independent expert reviewer; the Editor's decision is final.

This journal uses the Elsevier Article Transfer Service: an editor may recommend transferring a manuscript to a more suitable journal (with a chance to revise first); the receiving journal reviews the manuscript independently.
Write text in good English (American or British usage accepted, but not a mixture of the two).
No Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) code requirement is stated in the guide for authors.
Title should be concise and informative, avoiding abbreviations and formulae where possible (no character/word limit stated).

Where the family name may be ambiguous (e.g., a double name), indicate this clearly; affiliation footnotes use lower-case superscript letters, and a 'Present/permanent address' footnote (superscript Arabic numeral) may be used if an author has since moved.
The abstract must state the results as fully as possible, define crucial terms, and stand on its own with no numbered reference to the bibliography.

Provide a maximum of 6 keywords immediately after the abstract, using American spelling; avoid general/plural terms and multiple concepts (e.g., 'and', 'of'); be sparing with abbreviations (only those firmly established in the field).

Declaration of competing interest is required for all submissions, via Elsevier's declaration template/tool (do not convert the .docx template to another file type; choose the first option in the template if there is nothing to declare).

If generative AI/AI-assisted technology was used in the writing process, a 'Declaration of Generative AI and AI-assisted technologies in the writing process' section is required at the end of the manuscript (before the References list); not needed if there is nothing to disclose.

Role of the funding source: identify who funded the research and briefly describe their role in study design/data/writing/decision to submit (or state they had no such role); recommended wording: 'Funding: This work was supported by [funder] [grant number(s)]', or, if unfunded, 'This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.'
Research data sharing/linking is encouraged, not required; a CRediT/author-contribution statement is not mentioned in this journal's guide for authors.

figures.font: Arial, Courier, Times New Roman, or Symbol (or a similar-looking font)
notes: TIFF or JPEG for color/grayscale photographs (halftones, >=300 dpi) and for bitmapped line drawings (>=1000 dpi); TIFF or JPEG for combination bitmapped line/halftone art (>=500 dpi); EPS or PDF for vector drawings (embed all fonts).
Column widths are Elsevier's general defaults (the journal-specific guide does not override them): minimal size 30 mm, single column 90 mm, 1.5 column 140 mm, double column (full width) 190 mm.
Lettering should have a finished print size of about 7 pt for normal text and no smaller than 6 pt for subscript/superscript (rule of thumb, not a strict rule).

Do not supply screen-only formats (GIF, BMP, PICT, WPG), files that are too low in resolution, or graphics disproportionately large for their content; ensure color images are accessible to readers with impaired color vision.

Elsevier's image-manipulation policy: no feature within an image may be enhanced, obscured, moved, removed, or introduced; brightness/contrast/color-balance adjustments are acceptable as long as they do not obscure or eliminate information present in the original.
Supply captions separately from the illustration file; number illustrations according to their sequence in the text.

Submit tables as editable text, not images; place next to the relevant text or on separate page(s) at the end; number consecutively per their appearance in the text; avoid vertical rules and shading; place table notes below the table body.

In-text citations use bracketed numbers, e.g. '...as demonstrated [3,6]. Barnaby and Jones [8] obtained...'; the reference list is numbered but ordered alphabetically by the last name of the first author (not by order of citation).

Unpublished results and personal communications are not recommended in the reference list (mention them in the text instead); if listed, substitute the date with 'Unpublished results' or 'Personal communication'.

Preprints central to the work, or covering crucial developments not yet formally published, may be referenced if clearly marked as a preprint with a DOI; once formally published, cite the formal publication instead.
Data references are encouraged: cite datasets in the text and include a reference list entry (author(s), dataset title, repository, version, year, persistent identifier) prefixed with '[dataset]'.

Supplementary items (applications, images, sound clips, etc.) are published online exactly as received (e.g., Excel/PowerPoint files appear as such); switch off 'Track Changes' in Office files before submission; supply a concise descriptive caption for each item.

Video/animation files: preferred maximum size 150 MB per file, 1 GB total; provide a still image for each video; because video cannot be embedded in the print version, also provide text describing that content for print readers.
No explicit overall size cap for supplementary material is stated in the guide for authors.

Article types described in the guide for authors: Contribution (full-length, more than 7 journal pages / roughly 10+ manuscript pages, no stated upper limit), Note (short and self-contained, at most 7 journal pages / roughly 10 manuscript pages, expedited processing), and Perspectives (expository/survey articles accessible to a broad audience, presenting a unifying viewpoint on well-known or insufficiently-known topics). The journal also publishes occasional refereed Special Issues and Corrigenda (concise corrections to a prior article by the same authors).

Highlights are optional but highly encouraged (they increase discoverability via search engines): submit as a separate editable file named 'Highlights', with 3 to 5 bullet points, each a maximum of 85 characters including spaces.
Length: main text should not exceed 30 pages, in 11-point LaTeX format on US letter-size paper with 1-inch (25.4 mm) margins.
Authors of longer papers are advised to submit a 30-page version to Combinatorica with a link to a full version on arXiv.
Short Notes are welcome and are processed in an expedited fashion (no separate page limit stated for Notes).
Manuscripts are submitted via the editorial system EditFlow at https://ef.msp.org/submit/combinatorica -- not the generic Springer submission portal.

Final accepted version must be in TeX/LaTeX format; avoid complicated macros or non-standard packages/fonts, and delete unused packages/definitions -- a plain 'vanilla' LaTeX file is least error-prone when the journal typesets it.

It is desirable that theorems, lemmas, definitions, corollaries, examples, etc. be numbered consecutively with double Arabic numerals (e.g. Section 3 starts with Definition 3.1, then Remark 3.2, Theorem 3.3).
At final-version submission: affiliation and e-mail address required for each author, plus an abbreviated title of at most 35 characters to be used as the running head.
A brief abstract is required in the manuscript; no length limit stated.
The journal has a competing-interest policy in place (confirmed on the live Ethics & disclosures page); the journal is a COPE member and subscribes to its misconduct-handling principles.

Funding, data-availability, and author-contribution statements are not mentioned in the Combinatorica-specific Instructions to Authors document, unlike the generic Springer 'Instructions for Authors' template seen on other Springer journals.

Each figure must be supplied as a separate file, in a vector graphic format that can handle embedded fonts -- EPS or vector PDF only; the journal-specific instructions do not mention raster formats or dpi requirements.
The online version is published in color but the print version is converted to grayscale; figures must remain understandable in grayscale (e.g. avoid referring to colors in the running text).
No specific reference style is mandated in the Instructions to Authors document.
Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) codes -- both primary and secondary -- are required at final-version submission.
Submission portal is EditFlow (https://ef.msp.org/submit/combinatorica), distinct from Springer's standard Editorial Manager / online submission system referenced by other Springer math journals.

Journal is co-published by the Bolyai Society and Springer-Verlag; the paperpush-listed submission_guide URL https://combinatorica.hu/ is the society's own site (not fetched directly), separate from the Springer-hosted pages used for this data.
Style/presentation guidance: clarity is paramount, results should be made accessible to the non-specialist reader, with clear motivation, background, and exact references.
